intraday-tape-lab.sessionType=Trend day down; control=Mixed; vwap=774.66; gapPct=-0.02
items.method: Cross-read the dealer gamma regime and its flip and wall levels against the options-structure signed net-gamma sign, the options-flow lean and most-unusual prints, the market-heatmap breadth percentage versus its 60% threshold, and the intraday session type and VWAP with the VIX band, then judge whether short-gamma dealer positioning is being pressed toward a wall break or is likely to hold the range.
items.note: Dealer positioning has flipped to negative gamma this window: signed net gamma is about -$1.55B, SPY spot 773.38 sits just below the 775.05 flip, and the wall band is tight at 773/777 with a front expected move of only plus or minus 2.75. Under negative gamma, dealers hedge with the move rather than against it, so a break tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape reinforces a downside test: option flow is balanced overall at 42.1% calls (call premium $1.17B against put $1.61B), but the single most unusual print is a same-day SPY 775 put at $136.6M on 74.7x open interest sitting right on the 773 put wall, with a QQQ 732 put next. Breadth is narrow at 51.05% of 134 names, an -8.95-point shortfall to the 60% threshold, and the live SPY tape is a trend-day-down auction under mixed control with VWAP 774.66. VIX 15.19 is still low, so this is pressure rather than panic, but the setup argues that a slip through the 773 put wall would accelerate rather than fade, while the 777 call wall caps the upside.
items.title: Dealer gamma has flipped negative with heavy same-day puts pinned on the 773 put wall while breadth and the tape sag

inputs: global-rotation-lab.leader=EWS Singapore (90.1); next=EWT Taiwan (82.2); benchmark=ACWI; scored=13
items.method: Compare the sector rotation into and out tickers and the ETF-momentum and global-rotation leaders against the real-assets model scores and trends, tracking whether the equity-versus-hard-asset divergence is widening or closing versus the prior window.
items.note: Equity leadership is still concentrated but rotating within cyclicals: sector rotation is into XLK (Leading, acceleration +2.73) as XLI weakens and XLV leadership fades, ETF momentum is led by tech (VGT 34.47%) ahead of JMOM, SPMO, MTUM and QQQ, and the global board is topped by ex-US names EWS (Singapore, 90.1/100) and EWT (Taiwan, 82.2) versus ACWI. The real-assets book has firmed from the prior window but still trails: industrial copper (CPER 63.2) leads with broad commodities (DBC 56.2) and oil (USO 43.6) constructive, while gold (GLD 40.7) and silver (SLV 20.7) remain mixed and the bitcoin proxies are split, with BTC-USD 41.8 mixed and IBIT 33 in a downtrend. The read is a risk-on advance broadening slightly into commodities rather than a defensive rotation into monetary metals, so real assets stay a weak diversifier and only a partial confirmation source this window.
items.title: US-tech and ex-US equity leadership persists while real assets firm modestly but still lag
